tests.test: both DEVELOPMENT sources declare the legacy US Congress bill DTD
tests.fails_when: the corpus uses a different schema, so the structural predicate below would be asserted about elements this DTD does not define

tests.test: this corpus has NO <account> element -- the account level is appropriations-small
tests.fails_when: an <account> element exists, so the newer schema's structure should be used instead and the legacy predicate would be the wrong one

tests.test: the header is a CHILD ELEMENT here, never the attribute the prose examples abbreviate
tests.fails_when: some headers are attributes, so a child-only reader silently truncates the population

tests.test: a schema mismatch REFUSES rather than being read anyway
tests.fails_when: an unexpected DTD is parsed as though it were the legacy bill DTD

tests.test: CONSISTENCY ONLY -- the paired set carries no order inversion
tests.fails_when: the paired rows contradict themselves. NOTE this check CANNOT license the pairing rule: these rows were paired index-to-index, so a green result is guaranteed by construction. It is retained as a consistency assertion only

tests.test: the LICENSING evidence is independent of the pairing -- anchors alone, zero inversions
tests.fails_when: the independent anchors invert, so XML reading order does not correspond to physical print order and the ordinal pairing rule is unlicensed -- a STOP. This is the check the unique-occurrence subset (n=1 in 114-hr-2029/4) was far too small to make; x25 falsifies it in full, including the five bracketing negatives

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- a contradicted physical ordering IS detected as an inversion
tests.fails_when: the order check cannot go red, so its green result on the real material proves nothing

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- an extra XML occurrence REFUSES the whole group on count mismatch
tests.fails_when: a count mismatch is paired anyway, so the k-to-k rule would silently mis-associate a heading with a different physical occurrence

tests.test: ...and the refusal removes the ENTIRE group, not just the surplus
tests.fails_when: only the extra record is dropped, leaving the rest of an unverifiable group paired. Asserted as a direct property of the paired set rather than as an arithmetic identity, which would silently absorb any other refusal into the expected count

tests.test: the source population is BYTE-IDENTICAL with run_hybrid/run_extended/extract_anchors raising
tests.fails_when: an architecture path contributes to source enumeration, which A40.3 forbids -- and would mean N-A/N-B truth is derived from the thing under test

tests.test: ...and so is the na-source ranking's selected 8
tests.fails_when: ranking or selection consults H or X

tests.test: the sabotage is real -- calling a disabled path raises
tests.fails_when: the monkeypatch did not take, so the control passed because nothing was disabled

tests.test: N-A eligible population is at least 8
tests.fails_when: fewer than 8 independent N-A sources survive the bridge -- a STOP, not a reason to relax eligibility

tests.test: N-B eligible population is at least 8
tests.fails_when: fewer than 8 independent N-B sources survive the bridge
